page: The Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a dedicated bare metal server configured with an Intel Xeon E-2388G processor operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor provides 8 physical cores and 16 execution threads, supplemented by 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache. Memory provisioning stands at 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, allocating 8.0 GB of system memory per thread. The server integrates 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations highlight competitive single-threaded capabilities alongside memory-dense execution. The single-core Geekbench score reached 2184.0 and gzip single-threaded compression attained 36.27 GB/sec, placing both results in the upper tiers of evaluated systems. PassMark memory testing scored 3390.33, reflecting strong memory subsystem responsiveness. In contrast, uncached sequential memory bandwidth registered at 36.93 GB/sec for large-block reads and 19.38 GB/sec for writes, falling into lower benchmark percentiles. Multi-core performance aligns with expected 8-core bounds, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 10124.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 23271.22.

The hardware configuration provides substantial cost efficiency for operations that require dedicated bare-metal isolation combined with large memory capacities and fast NVMe storage, without the financial overhead of dual-socket platforms. While the 8-core CPU limits total parallel throughput in heavily concurrent computing environments, the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and low-latency local storage make the platform well suited for relational database hosting, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, enterprise web serving, and single-threaded batch data transformations.

It features 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering an 8.0 GB per-thread allocation, alongside 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and zero GPUs. Benchmark testing reveals strong single-thread efficiency, achieving 36.27 GB/sec in gzip compression and a Geekbench single-core score of 2184.0, while PassMark memory performance places in the top decile. Sustained uncached memory bandwidth remains comparatively limited at 36.93 GB/sec read and 19.38 GB/sec write. Multi-core compute yields steady midrange results, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 10124.0 and 16.84 million Redis SET operations per second. The server provides dedicated hardware isolation optimal for memory-heavy databases, caching, and IOPS-intensive application serving.
